headline: The land *nobody wants*
intent: Two colonial border lines that disagree, and the strange result: one triangle both Egypt and Sudan claim, and one patch of desert neither will touch, because claiming it means giving up the other.

post.premise: A patch of Sahara that neither Egypt nor Sudan claims, because of two border lines drawn a century ago

youtube.title: Bir Tawil: the land nobody wants 🛰️
youtube.description:
On the border of Egypt and Sudan there is a patch of desert the size of a small country that neither side claims. Not forgotten, not unknown, deliberately refused. The reason is two lines drawn by the same empire a few years apart, and what each one hands to the other side. This map story shows both lines and why claiming this land would cost more than it is worth.
Would you claim it? Tell us below.

vo.text: Between Egypt and Sudan there is a piece of desert that nobody claims. Not forgotten. Refused.
In 1899 Britain drew the border along the 22nd parallel. A straight line, east to west.
Three years later it drew a second line, following the tribes instead: a bend north by the sea, a bend south in the desert.

research.topic: Bir Tawil, a ~2,060 km² area between Egypt and Sudan claimed by neither, exists because the 1899 Anglo-Egyptian Condominium boundary (22°N) and the 1902 administrative boundary disagree; each state asserts the line that gives it the larger Hala'ib Triangle on the Red Sea, so neither can claim Bir Tawil.

myths.myth: Bir Tawil is unclaimed because nobody knows it exists.
myths.reality: Both Egypt and Sudan know it; claiming it would mean accepting the boundary line that hands the far larger Hala'ib Triangle to the other side.

landscape.our_gap: Bir Tawil Shorts are talking heads about 'the last unclaimed land' and self-declared kingdoms; nobody draws both lines on the satellite map and shows, in one frame, why claiming the small patch costs the coastal triangle.

brit_halaib.title: Ḥalāʾib Triangle
brit_halaib.notes: Area of about 20,580 km² on the Red Sea coast; 1899 agreement set the political boundary at 22°N; 1902 administrative boundary gave the area to Sudan; administered by Egypt, claimed by Sudan.

wiki_birtawil.title: Bir Tawil
wiki_birtawil.notes: About 2,060 km²; terra nullius; result of the 1899 (22°N) and 1902 boundaries; claiming it would forfeit the claim to the Hala'ib Triangle.

wiki_halaib.title: Hala'ib Triangle
wiki_halaib.notes: 20,580 km²; towns Hala'ib, Abu Ramad, Shalateen; Egypt administers since the 1990s; Sudan claims; 1902 line placed it under Khartoum.

condominium.publisher: Anglo-Egyptian Condominium Agreement (19 January 1899), text via Wikisource
condominium.title: Agreement between Her Britannic Majesty's Government and the Government of His Highness the Khedive of Egypt relative to the future administration of the Sudan
condominium.notes: Article I: the word Sudan means all territories south of the 22nd parallel of latitude.

guardian.title: Welcome to the land that no country wants (2016)

ibs18.publisher: US Department of State, Office of the Geographer
ibs18.title: International Boundary Study No. 18: Sudan – United Arab Republic (Egypt) Boundary (27 July 1962)
ibs18.notes: Official boundary study: the 1899 Condominium boundary at 22°N, the 1902 administrative boundary and the two areas (Hala'ib north of 22°N administered from Khartoum; Bir Tawil south of it administered from Cairo).
